subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the reaction N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, how many moles of NH3 form from 6 mol of H2 (excess N2)?
questions.explain: From the 3:2 ratio, 6 mol H2 produces (2/3) × 6 = 4 mol NH3.

questions.q: In the reaction 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, which is the limiting reagent if 0.10 mol Mg reacts with 0.10 mol O2?
questions.explain: The 2:1 ratio means 0.10 mol Mg needs only 0.05 mol O2; Mg runs out first so it is limiting.

questions.q: 25.0 cm3 of NaOH is exactly neutralised by 20.0 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 HCl (1:1). What is the concentration of the NaOH?
questions.explain: Moles HCl = 0.100 × 20.0/1000 = 0.00200 mol = moles NaOH; concentration = 0.00200/0.0250 = 0.080 mol/dm3.

questions.q: What is the empirical formula of a compound containing 40% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass? (Ar: C=12, H=1, O=16)
questions.explain: Dividing by Ar gives ratios 3.33 : 6.7 : 3.33 = 1 : 2 : 1, so the empirical formula is CH2O.

questions.q: How many moles of HCl are in 50.0 cm3 of 0.200 mol/dm3 solution?
At 273 K and 101 kPa, what volume does 0.5 mol of ideal gas occupy? (Molar gas volume ≈ 22.4 dm3 at stp)
questions.explain: Volume = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 dm3 at standard temperature and pressure.

questions.q: 25.0 cm3 of a NaOH solution requires 22.5 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 HCl for neutralisation (1:1). What is the NaOH concentration?
questions.explain: Moles HCl = 0.100 × 22.5/1000 = 0.00225 mol = moles NaOH; concentration = 0.00225/0.0250 = 0.0900 mol/dm3.

questions.q: What is the Mr of CuSO4·5H2O? (Ar: Cu=63.5, S=32, O=16, H=1)
When a hydrated salt is heated to constant mass, the mass lost corresponds to:
options: The gas given off in a reaction
The mass of water of crystallisation driven off
An amount that cannot be determined
questions.explain: On heating a hydrated salt, the mass lost equals the mass of water of crystallisation driven off.

questions.q: How many moles are in 4.4 g of CO2? (Mr = 44)
questions.explain: Moles = mass/Mr = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol.

questions.q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 8.0 g but only 6.0 g is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explain: Percentage yield = (actual/theoretical) × 100 = (6.0/8.0) × 100 = 75%.

questions.q: What is the atom economy for the desired product MgO in 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO?
questions.explain: MgO is the only product, so all atoms end up in the desired product and the atom economy is 100%.

questions.q: Using pV = nRT, what is the volume of 1 mol of gas at 300 K and 100 kPa (R = 8.31 J K-1 mol-1)?
In CaCO3 → CaO + CO2, what mass of CaO (Mr=56) forms from 10 g of CaCO3 (Mr=100)?
questions.explain: Moles CaCO3 = 10/100 = 0.10; this gives 0.10 mol CaO; mass = 0.10 × 56 = 5.6 g.

questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in NH4NO3? (Ar: N=14, H=1, O=16; Mr=80)
questions.explain: There are 2 nitrogen atoms (28); (28/80) × 100 = 35%.

questions.q: A 4.0 g sample of magnesium (Ar=24) reacts completely. How many moles of Mg is this?
questions.explain: Moles = mass/Ar = 4.0/24 = 0.167 mol.

questions.q: Which expression correctly gives the number of moles from a titration volume V (cm3) and concentration c (mol/dm3)?
questions.explain: Moles = concentration × volume in dm3 = c × V/1000 when V is in cm3.

questions.q: How many moles of oxygen atoms are in 0.5 mol of Al2(SO4)3?
questions.explain: Each formula unit contains 12 oxygen atoms, so 0.5 × 12 = 6 mol of oxygen atoms.

questions.q: What is the concentration of a solution made by dissolving 0.5 mol of NaCl in water to give 250 cm3 of solution?
questions.explain: Concentration = moles/volume = 0.5 / 0.250 = 2 mol/dm3.

questions.q: How many moles are present in 12 g of carbon-12? (Ar = 12)
questions.explain: Moles = mass/Mr = 12/12 = 1 mol.

questions.q: What mass of NaOH (Mr = 40) is required to make 2.00 dm3 of 0.25 mol/dm3 solution?
What mass of CaCO3 (Mr = 100) is needed to provide 0.25 mol?
questions.explain: Mass = moles × Mr = 0.25 × 100 = 25 g.

questions.q: In a titration, 24.0 cm3 of 0.0500 mol/dm3 H2SO4 reacts with NaOH: H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2H2O. How many moles of NaOH react?
questions.explain: Moles H2SO4 = 0.0500 × 24.0/1000 = 0.0012; NaOH is in a 2:1 ratio, so 0.0024 mol.

questions.q: What is the molar mass of a gas if 0.50 g occupies 0.40 dm3 at stp (molar volume 22.4 dm3/mol)?
What volume of 2.0 mol/dm3 stock solution is needed to make 500 cm3 of 0.50 mol/dm3 solution by dilution?
What is the atom economy for producing H2 in the reaction Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2? (Mr: H2=2, ZnCl2=136)
questions.explain: Atom economy = (Mr desired/total Mr of products) × 100 = (2/138) × 100 ≈ 1.4%.

questions.q: How many molecules are in 2 mol of water? (NA = 6.02 × 10^23)
questions.explain: Number = moles × NA = 2 × 6.02 × 10^23 = 1.204 × 10^24 molecules.

questions.q: How many grams of water are lost when 0.10 mol of MgSO4·7H2O is fully dehydrated? (Mr H2O = 18)
questions.explain: Each mole contains 7 mol water; 0.10 × 7 × 18 = 12.6 g of water lost.

questions.q: A gas occupies 2.40 dm3 at 100 kPa and 300 K. Using pV = nRT (R = 8.31), how many moles are present?
A compound has empirical formula CH2 and Mr = 56. What is its molecular formula? (Ar: C=12, H=1)
questions.explain: Empirical mass = 14; 56/14 = 4, so the molecular formula is C4H8.
